report.note: Eight fixed epochs on eight groups; training-fit cases are memorization checks, transfer probes are not training targets; validation loss is not meaning preservation or style quality. Test split untouched by optimization and evaluation.

diagnostics.limitations: Exact textual differences measure responsiveness, not stylistic quality. Identical output can be appropriate for some inputs. One deterministic generation per condition. Training-fit outputs are memorization diagnostics. Transfer probes are small and lack independent ratings; none establish generalization alone.

semantic_review.reviewer: Assistant editorial review, unblinded; not independent human evaluation
semantic_review.summary: Familiar targets are learned (31/40 exact matches), but transfer remains unreliable: 10 clear meaning/stance failures and 8 minor or ambiguous shifts in 40 fresh outputs. One clear omission also occurred in the 40 familiar outputs. Not deployed.

rubric.0: Changed or omitted claim, role, referent, attribution or stance

style_findings: Characteristic vocabulary and rhetorical structures learned on familiar inputs, beyond capitals.
Role-question structure transfers to new names and amount, but explicit payment-after-repair relation is weakened.
Political criticism uses the observed nickname at high levels; praise incorrectly receives the nickname at 100.
Uncertainty is preserved in several strong-style outputs; level 50 drops the parcel referent.
Distinct outputs at all cases do not imply five perceptually calibrated or monotonically increasing levels.
semantic_review.limitations: All 80 after outputs reviewed against original inputs; before outputs only spot reviewed for meaning. No before/after semantic accuracy claim. Training-fit results reflect deliberate memorization. Eight transfer inputs with one deterministic generation each do not establish population accuracy.

deployment: Experimental only; existing archive and prompt-only slider modes remain unchanged.
